findings.reason: The protected Python solution implements read(buf, n) for multiple calls by maintaining a persistent 4-character temporary buffer, position index, and available count on the Solution instance. It consumes unread cached characters first before calling read4 to fetch subsequent 4-character chunks. The solution runs in O(n) total time for n returned characters and O(1) auxiliary space; no candidate is required.

Instance-level persistence of position and available indices preserves unused buffer suffixes across independent calls to read, guaranteeing seamless stream continuation without losing or duplicating characters.

Each character is fetched into the temporary buffer once and copied to an output buffer once, yielding O(n) total time for n returned characters across calls. Auxiliary space is O(1) for the 4-character instance buffer and scalar pointers. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts destination buffer buf (List[str]) and request length n, populating buf in-place and returning the integer count of actual characters read across multiple calls.

The approach accurately details instance-level state persistence, pre-fetch cache consumption, on-demand read4 refilling, and O(n) time / O(1) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover single-call state erasure hazards, per-character read4 primitive over-call defects, full-file buffering memory costs, partial chunk exhaustion stops, pre-EOF short reads, and post-EOF zero-length query behavior.
